issue.done_when:
- [ ] Two new `[build]` triggers whose titles cite the same GOV id arrive in one check, with free slots: the first starts and the second is held. (The builder started this check counts as live.)
- [ ] A `[build]` trigger is held while a live builder (heartbeat, or launcher entry with no heartbeat yet) is on an issue whose title shares a GOV id. It starts on the first check after that builder stops, if no open PR also holds it.
- [ ] A `[build]` trigger is held while an open PR, draft or not, closes an issue whose title shares a GOV id. It starts once that PR is merged or closed.
- [ ] Issues whose titles share no GOV id, or cite none, run side by side as today. A GOV id cited only in the body doesn't hold.
- [ ] `[respond]`, `[review]`, `[record]` and `[answer]` triggers are never held by this rule.
- [ ] The hold shows in `swarm inbox` with its reason, as GOV-0010 holds do.
- [ ] The `launcher/watch.py` module docstring and `launcher/README.md` describe the rule.
- [ ] Tests cover each case above. `triggers()` stays pure; the check can sit in `start_tick` next to the ceiling check, using data `gather()` already reads (issue titles, PR `closes`).
